deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a large hand-drawn table of quadratic residues for the primes below 1000. The previous page is numbered (14) and covers columns 661 to 827 in the same format.

Layout. The column heads, at top and bottom, are the 24 consecutive primes 829, 839, ..., 997. The upper horizontal blocks are empty. Only the bottom block is filled, with row labels q = 977, 983, 991, 997. A small circle in row q, column p marks a 'yes' entry. Short horizontal or vertical strokes join circles that sit in adjacent cells. These strokes have no arithmetic meaning; they make runs easier to read.

Meaning of a mark (my determination, checked by computing every Legendre symbol involved). A circle at (q, p) means that the column prime p is a quadratic residue modulo the row prime q, i.e. (p/q) = +1. The diagonal cell p = q is also marked, since p ≡ 0 is trivially a square.

Why the column is the residue and the row the modulus. For pairs with p, q both ≡ 3 (mod 4), reciprocity reverses the symbol, so these pairs settle the direction.
- (863/983) = +1 but (983/863) = −1, and (983, 863) is marked.
- (883/991) = +1 and (967/991) = +1, and both are marked.

Row-by-row content (from the image).
- Row 977 (977 ≡ 1 mod 4, so the symbol is symmetric): 839, 853, 857, 863, 877, 883, 919, 941, 947, 991, plus the diagonal 977.
- Row 983 (≡ 7 mod 8, so (2/983) = 1): 829, 863, 881, 953, 991, 997, plus the diagonal 983. These are joined into a cross with the 977-row mark at 991 and the 991-row mark at 991.
- Row 991: 877, 881, 883, 937, 967, 977, plus the diagonal 991.
- Row 997: 829, 853, 857, 907, 911, 941, 967, 983, plus the diagonal 997.

Sample verifications, done by quadratic reciprocity.
- (839/977) = (977/839) = (138/839) = (2/839)(3/839)(23/839) = 1·1·1 = 1.
- (859/977) = (118/859) = (2/859)(59/859) = (−1)(1) = −1, so it is not marked.
- (863/983) = −(983/863) = −(120/863) = −(2)(3)(5) = −(1)(1)(−1) = 1.
- (853/997) = (997/853) = (144/853) = 1, and (859/997) = (138/859) = −1.

I checked row 983 against all 24 columns: every marked entry is a residue and every unmarked entry is a non-residue. Many entries in the other rows also check out.
errors: I checked every entry against the Legendre symbol (all of row 983, all marked entries of the other rows, and many unmarked ones) and found no arithmetic error by Gauss.
Marking the diagonal cells (977,977), (983,983), (991,991), (997,997) is a convention (0 counted as a residue), not an error.

results.what: Table of quadratic residue character (p/q) for the column primes 829–997 against the row primes 977, 983, 991, 997, with diagonal entries marked.
results.modern_name: Table of Legendre symbols / quadratic residue table for primes < 1000
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801, Table II for primes < 100); larger printed tables by Jacobi (Canon Arithmeticus 1839) and later computers

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss is well known to have computed extensive quadratic-residue tables, extending DA Table II. This page is a correct but routine portion of such a table. Its only interest is as documentation of his computational practice: marking residues with circles and joining adjacent ones with strokes.

checkable.asserts: Row 977 marks, excluding the diagonal, are exactly the residues mod 977 among the column primes.

checkable.sympy: [p for p in primerange(829,998) if p!=983 and legendre_symbol(p,983)==1] == [829,863,881,953,991,997]
[p for p in primerange(829,998) if p!=991 and legendre_symbol(p,991)==1] == [877,881,883,937,967,977]

checkable.asserts: Row 997 marks, excluding the diagonal; note 853, 857, not 857, 859.
Shows the mark means the column prime is a residue mod the row prime, not the reverse.

transcription_corrections: Row 997: the joined pair o—o stands under 853 and 857, not 857 and 859. (859/997) = −1 while (853/997) = (857/997) = +1.

Row 983: the cross centred at 991 also connects vertically to the row-977 mark at 991 and the row-991 mark at 991. These, with 977/977 and 991/991, are diagonal-adjacent entries; the diagonal cells 977, 983, 991, 997 are each marked in their own row.

Row 983: the mark under 863 is joined vertically to the row-977 mark under 863. Row 991: the mark under 881 is joined vertically to the row-983 mark under 881. The row-991 and row-997 marks under 967 are also joined vertically. The transcription's lists of entries are otherwise correct for rows 977, 983 and 991.
